measured_findings: The verification root is a 2-of-2 attester set: signatureThreshold == getNumEnabledAttesters == 2.
Every governance role we could read is an externally owned account: both contract owners, the attesterManager, and both pausers.
Neither TokenMessenger nor MessageTransmitter is an ERC1967 proxy; the implementation and admin slots are zero.

The only value limit we found is burnLimitsPerMessage, 1,000,000 USDC. It caps a single message on the sending side and does not accumulate, so it bounds no aggregate: N messages at the cap pass N million.
Role separation is real where it matters: isEnabledAttester returns false for both the attesterManager and the owner, so the party that controls the verification root is not part of it.

TokenMinter.sol mint() has no amount gate; only burn() uses onlyWithinBurnLimit. TokenMessenger mint path calls minter.mint with no aggregate/per-message bound (github.com/circlefin/evm-cctp-contracts).
Upgrade path without a proxy: bytecode is immutable; owner EOAs can rotate attesters/localMinter pointers but cannot swap implementation in place — replacement is a migration.
verdict_reasoning: On the destination side a message is verified against the attester set and then minted; we found no configurable parameter that gates inbound value per message and can be changed without redeployment. burnLimitsPerMessage sits on the send path. Under the definition fixed in SEPARABILITY-CHECK.md this is no position rather than a removable one. The authority condition of separability is therefore satisfied; what is absent is a position, not independence.
